sentences.text: This interlocutory application has been filed by the insurance company in M.A. No. 827 of 2015 for taking report of Investigator appointed by it along with report of license authority on record according to which the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving license at the time of accident.
The reason for not filing the said report before tribunal is mentioned that the report was received on 20.08.15 after passing the award on 29.04.15.
Learned counsel for the claimants vehemently opposed the application and prayed for its dismissal.
Heard and perused the available record.

There is nothing on record to show that insurance company had applied due diligence and took necessary step to obtain the said report when the trial was going on before tribunal and even after applying due diligence company was not able to produce the report before the tribunal.
Under these circumstances, there is no ground to take the said report as additional evidence.

Consequently, I.A.
No. 4645 of 2015 is dismissed.

Since common question of law is involved in aforesaid M.A. Nos. 772 of 2015 and 827 of 2015,
therefore, they are heard analogously and are decided by this common judgment.
M.A. No. 772 of 2015 has been filed by the claimants whereas M.A. No. 827 of 2015 has been filed by the insurance company.
For the sake of convenience, facts mentioned in M.A. No. 772 of 2015 are taken into consideration.

These appeals have been filed assailing the award dated 29.4.2015 passed by Fifth Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gwalior (M.P.) in Claim Case No. 111/2014 filed by the appellants (respondents No. 1 to 5 in M.A. No. 827 of 2015) for grant of compensation on account of death of deceased Pankaj Singh in a road traffic accident occurred on 02.9.2012 involving offending vehicle Truck bearing registration No.MP09-KD-0774.

At the time of accident, respondent No. 1 (respondent No. 6 in M.A. No. 827 of 2015) was the driver and respondent No. 2 (respondent No. 7 in M.A. No. 827 of 2015) was the owner of the offending vehicle and the vehicle was insured with respondent No. 3 (appellant in M.A. No. 827 of 2015) - insurance company.
Respondents No. 1 and 2 - driver and owner of the offending vehicle remained absent before learned claims tribunal and
were proceeded ex-parte.

Insurance company filed its written statement and denied the averments made in the claim petition and further stated that at the time of accident, offending vehicle was being plied in breach of policy terms and conditions, therefore, insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.

Learned claims tribunal after hearing both the parties and going through the evidence available on record partially allowed the claim petition of the claimants and awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.85,72,304/- which was directed to be paid by the respondents - driver, owner and, insurance company of the offending vehicle jointly and severely.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the insurance company by filing M.A. No. 827 of 2015 argued that there was breach in the terms and conditions of the insurance policy because at the time of accident, driver of the offending vehicle was not carrying valid and effective driving license, therefore, insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.
It is further argued that the spot map clearly indicates that the said accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Scorpio driver namely Pramod Kumar in which deceased was travelling.
Further argument is that learned claims tribunal has wrongly assessed the monthly and yearly income of deceased Pankaj Singh on the basis of income tax return.
Learned claims tribunal should have taken the average income of last three years from the date of death of deceased Pankaj Singh.

Learned counsel for the insurance company further argued that learned claims tribunal has wrongly mentioned the income of the deceased as Rs.6,35,780/- in the assessment year 2012-13 instead it should have been Rs.5,35,780/-.
Further argument is that compensation in conventional heads as well as for future loss of income has also wrongly been awarded.
Hence, prayed to set aside the impugned award.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the claimants argued that on the basis of statement of AW-3 B.L. Meena, who was the Income-tax Inspector and proved the income tax record of the deceased,
learned claims tribunal has rightly assessed the monthly and annual income of deceased Pankaj Singh.
It is further argued that deceased died in the year 2012 on 02.9.2012 and income-tax return was up to March, 2012.
After March, 2012, deceased worked for about six months for which documents have also been filed and that income has rightly been included by learned claims tribunal in the impugned award.

However, by filing M.A. No. 772 of 2015, learned counsel for the claimants have submitted that the compensation amount awarded by learned claims tribunal is on the lesser side, therefore, the same be enhanced.
Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the available record.

In the case, during trial, insurance company has not adduced any evidence to prove that at the time of accident, driver of the offending vehicle was not carrying valid and effective driving license or offending vehicle was being plied without permit and fitness certificate.
It is well settled that the burden is on the insurance company to prove the defence taken by it.
Since the company has not discharged it's burden; therefore, there is no ground to exonerate the insurance company to pay the compensation.

So far as contributory negligence of the driver of Scorpio in which deceased was travelling is concerned, in this case on the basis of evidence of eye-witness Pramod Kumar @ Banti (AW-4), it is apparent that the accident occurred on account of rash and negligent driving of respondent No. 1 - Pappi Singh Rajpoot, driver of the offending vehicle.
Insurance Company has not adduced any evidence to contradict the case of claimants.
Even, Pappi, driver of the offending vehicle, did not appear before the learned claims tribunal to contradict the version of the eye witness in respect to details of accident.
Statement of eye-witness Pramod (AW-4) remained unchallenged in his cross-examination.
Therefore, learned claims tribunal has rightly held that the accident occurred on account of rash and negligent driving of driver of the offending vehicle Truck bearing registration No. MP09-KD-0774.

sentences.text: 5 On the basis of evidence adduced by the claimants, deceased Pankaj Singh was doing the business of transportation and building work under the name of Om Sai Constructions.
As per pan card Ex.P-7 and Income Tax Returns Ex.P-12 and P-13 date of birth of deceased Pankaj is 13.18.1979.

However,
in the Postmortem Report, the age of the deceased is mentioned as 35 years.

In view of the above,
learned claims tribunal has rightly held that the deceased at the time of accident was between 33 to 35 years.
As per the oral evidence of claimant Laxmi Kushwah, wife of the deceased, her husband was earning Rs.7,00,000/- per annum from the work of Om Sai Constructions.
Exh.P-10 is the registration certificate of Om Sai Constructions.
Her statement is supported by documents Exh.P-7 to P-18.
Claimant Laxmi Kushwah has also proved work order and other relevant documents regarding the work done by deceased as per Exh.P-14 to P-17.

Claimants have also examined AW-3 B.L. Meena,
who was the Income Tax Inspector.
This witness has proved the Income Tax Returns of deceased Pankaj Singh which are Exh.P-12, P-13 and P-20.

On the basis of Income Tax Returns, learned claims tribunal has rightly observed that the income of the deceased in the financial year 2010-11 was Rs.4,08,572/- (Exh.P-13/C), in the financial year 2011-12 was Rs.5,97,506/- (Exh.P-12/C) and in the financial year 2012-13, it was Rs.6,35,780/- (Exh.P-13).

The claimants have also filed documents to prove that in the year 2012 after the assessment of income tax in the month of March,
deceased had worked and earned income before death.
No cogent evidence has been adduced by the insurance company to contradict the documentary evidence adduced by the claimants.
In view of the above, learned claims tribunal has rightly held that at the time of accident, annual income of the deceased was Rs.6,35,780/-.
Now the question is what would be the just and proper compensation?

In view of the aforesaid discussion as well as in the light of the case laws of National Insurance Company vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors.; 2017 ACJ 2700) as well as Smt. Sarla Verma & Ors. vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors.; AIR 2009 SC 3104, considering the annual income of the deceased to be Rs.6,35,780/-, dependency 3/4 (Rs.635780 x 3/4 = 4,76,835), future prospect @ 40% (476835 x 40/100 = 190734), multiplier of 16 [(476835 + 190734) x 16 = Rs.1,06,81,104/-), and Rs.70,000/- in other heads, total compensation amount comes to Rs.1,07,51,104/-.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As such, the total amount awarded to the claimants is enhanced from Rs.85,72,304/- to Rs.1,07,51,104/-.

The enhanced amount comes to Rs.21,78,800/- (Rupees Twenty One Lakh Seventy Eight Thousand Eight Hundred only), with interest at the rate as fixed by the tribunal in the award which is directed to be paid to the claimants by the insurance company in the same apportionment as directed by the claims tribunal.
The enhanced amount of compensation Rs.21,78,800/- shall be payable to the claimants within 12 weeks from the date of production of a certified copy of this order.
Rest of the award impugned passed by the Tribunal shall remain intact.

If the enhanced amount of compensation is in excess to the valuation of appeal, the difference of the Court fee (if not already paid) shall be deposited by the claimants within four weeks' from today and proof thereof shall be submitted before the Registry.
Thereafter, Registry shall issue the certified copy of the order passed today.
